newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends weaker under heavy prompt supply.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends weaker under heavy prompt supply.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures were pulled lower on Monday by a glut of prompt North Sea barrels on the physical market, brokers said.
May Brent closed 41 cents down at $19.58 a barrel, with more than ten cents of losses made in a burst of selling led by a Wall Street trading house shortly before the close.
Brokers said that a well supplied physical Brent market in Europe, and intermonth spreads trading in contango on the cash Brent market were keeping up the pressure on futures.
"The physical glut in Europe, illustrated by the discount on Dated Brent, continues to weigh on the market," said brokers Prudential Bache in their daily report.
Support breaks in the $19.70/75 area triggered technical selling stops which helped to fuel the downward move, brokers said.
And a poor performance by NYMEX unleaded gasoline, the key market leader in the run-up to the summer driving season, compounded the bearish tone this side of the Atlantic, they added.
April NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures shed over one cent a gallon to close at 66.45 cents a gallon.
Weak fundamentals eclipsed any bullish impact of disruptions to crude production in Nigeria, dealers said.
Shell Nigeria said a dispute between rival villagers caused the weekend shutdown of five pumping stations which cut output through the Forcados crude export system by 100,000 bpd.
But traders said that that a supply cushion of 1.8 million barrels of Forcados held by Shell should shield against disruptions to exports.
A spokesman for the company said it would be able to meet all of its March export commitments.
Earlier, IPE April gas oil ended Monday unchanged at $170.75 a tonne, while the weakening of crude futures pushed out the crack spread, a rough indicator of refining margins.
"There's no real strength in gas oil, it's just Brent is ultra weak," said one broker.
